title: Chapter 3: Beneath the Hospital
notes: Revised CH03 (Authorized Inspection and Verification). Owner-approved first-entry premise; new dialogue proposed and pending narrative review. Scenes 01-02: inspection notice and security briefing. Clinical coverage, audit summary and clinical scope are each completed before departure; no entry without coverage, approval and a life-safety assessment. The major corridor-loop reveal belongs to Chapter 4 Scene 09 and is not preempted. Scenes 03-04 (Descent, First actual entry into Ward Zero): the team goes down through the security wing's service hatch (the restricted lift's historic landing has no floor choice yet, so the screenplay's 'service elevator' is staged as the Facilities hatch and stair). Facilities clears the isolated circuit and opens the sealed corridor's end; inside the threshold the player compares maps, checks signage, documents the entrance and verifies the return route. Restricted patient records are not searched. Anomaly states stay at their ordinary defaults.

objectives.text: Naomi has an inspection notice for you at the nursing station. Settle your clinical work before you go.
Attend Marcus Hale's security briefing at the psychiatrist's office.
Go down with Hale and Facilities: through the ward entry, the maintenance room and the service hatch.
Wait for Facilities to clear the isolated circuit at the end of the mechanical corridor.
Inside the threshold: compare the maps, check the signage, document the entrance and verify the way back.

staff_lines.text: Ward entry, maintenance room, hatch. We meet you at the bottom of the stair.
Stay with the team, keep to the marked route, and we all come back the way we went in.
Briefing's when your ward is covered, Doctor. Not before.
Maps are on the desk when you're ready.
Your patients are covered. Go read your old floor plans.

interactions.title: Naomi Bennett: inspection notice
interactions.body:
Bennett: You've got an inspection briefing. Apparently your day job now includes reading old floor plans.

The notice: Security and Facilities will inspect the historic-access discrepancy. You attend as clinical liaison for the transfer workflow. Clinical coverage must be in place before departure.

options.label: Confirm who covers your patients while you're away
options.response:
Bennett: The ward doctor has your list and I'm on until handover. Anything urgent goes to them, not to you underground.

Clinical coverage confirmed.

options.label: Read the audit summary attached to the notice
options.response: The summary lists what Chapter 2 left open: an inactive credential in the transfer-request audit, export versions that disagree on a date, an unwatched door found ajar and a witness who heard but did not see. Nothing in it is resolved.

options.label: "Only the part related to clinical transfers."
options.response:
Bennett: Good. We'd hate to lose another psychiatrist to Facilities.

Scope recorded: you attend for the transfer-workflow question only. The building survey belongs to Security and Facilities.

options.label: Leave now and sort out coverage later
options.response: Bennett: No. Nobody leaves this ward uncovered, inspection or not.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: security briefing
interactions.body:
Hale has the current and historic maps side by side. A Facilities engineer has marked the approved areas, the radio channel and the stop conditions.

Hale: This is an authorized inspection, not a tour. Nobody enters alone; nobody opens an uncleared door.

Engineer: The old drawings weren't consistently revised. We'll establish what exists before we draw conclusions.

options.label: "What is the specific clinical question?"
options.response: Hale: Whether an obsolete code is still being routed through patient-transfer software. The building survey is ours.

options.label: Offer to go ahead and check the W0-B door yourself
options.response: Hale: Read the first line again. Nobody enters alone.

options.label: Review the boundaries, stop conditions and return route
options.response:
Boundaries reviewed: marked route only; stop on any loss of contact, unsafe air or structure; return by the entry sequence logged on the way in.

Hale: Entry approval and the Facilities life-safety check are signed. We go down together from the service lift.

interactions.unavailable_body: Hale is waiting for your ward to be covered.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: going down
interactions.body: Hale: Coverage confirmed, approval signed, life-safety check done. We go down through the maintenance hatch in the security wing. Facilities has the key; you're on the team pass.

options.label: Go down with the team
options.response: Team pass logged: ward entry and maintenance access for this inspection only. The restricted lift, W0-B and every uncleared door stay locked.

interactions.title: Bottom of the service stair
interactions.body:
The engineer logs the time and level at the stair foot. Motor noise from the plant, administrative labels, a maintenance inspection tag dated last month.

Engineer: Renovations changed the levels. The old plan's 'ground' isn't our current ground.

options.label: Log the level mismatch as something wrong with the building
options.response: Engineer: It's a drawing convention, not a fault. Write down what's different, not what it means.

options.label: "So the drawing might differ without anything being wrong."
options.response:
Engineer: Exactly.

Logged: current and historic level datums differ; no conclusion drawn.

interactions.unavailable_body: A stairwell fuse board, isolated and tagged.
interactions.completed_body: Inspection log: level datums differ between plan editions; no conclusion drawn.

interactions.title: Facilities clearance
interactions.body:
The engineer tests the isolated circuit and the air at the end of the sealed corridor. Hale radios control.

Hale: This area isn't in clinical service. Keep within the marked route.

options.label: Go on ahead to the brick end while they test
options.response: Hale: Nobody goes past this board until Facilities says so. Stay with us.

options.label: Wait for clearance, then go in together
options.response:
Engineer: Circuit isolated, air's fine, structure's sound. Opening the end now.

The infill at the end of the sealed corridor is taken down along a marked line. Behind it, a threshold room.

interactions.unavailable_body: An isolated circuit board. Facilities will check it.
interactions.completed_body: Clearance logged: circuit isolated, air and structure checked, threshold opened for the authorized team.

interactions.title: The threshold
interactions.body:
Heavy doorframes, faded institutional paint, empty fixtures. A stencil reads LOWER LEVEL B. An enamel plate is fixed beside the inner door.

You: Was this designated W0-B?

Engineer: The archival plan says so. We'll verify physical markers.

options.label: Compare the current map with the historic plan
options.response: The historic plan shows this threshold and a corridor beyond; the current map shows nothing below the sealed corridor. Logged as a plan-edition difference.

options.label: Check the authorized signage and markers
options.response: Stencils read LOWER LEVEL B and SERVICE B. The plate's wording matches the archival plan's room schedule. No sign uses the W0-B code itself; the designation remains the plan's.

options.label: Document the entrance condition
options.response: Documented with the time: inner door closed, frame intact, dust undisturbed except along the team's marked line, one radiator, one lamp working.

options.label: Verify the return route back to the sealed corridor
options.response: Hale walks it with you: threshold, opened infill, sealed corridor, mechanical corridor, stair. One route, physically continuous, marked.

interactions.unavailable_body: An enamel plate beside a closed inner door.
interactions.completed_body: Entry documented: plans compared, signage checked, condition recorded, return route verified.

interactions.title: Observation room records
interactions.body:
An old observation log lies on the desk.

Hale: Not ours to read. Historic patient records go to Records under its own authority, not into an inspection notebook.

options.label: Open it anyway
options.response: Hale: No. Leave it where it is. If it matters, Records will request it properly.

sign_out.title: Clinical handoff
sign_out.undocumented_message: Outstanding clinical review still requires an appropriate handoff.
